data.Table Header: Recommendation Table 1 -Recommendations for history taking, risk factor assessment, and resting electrocardiogram in individuals with suspected chronic coronary syndrome (see also Evidence Table 1)
data.Section Header: History taking and risk factor assessment
data.Recommendations: In individuals reporting symptoms of suspected myocardial ischaemic origin, a detailed assessment of cardiovascular risk factors, medical history, and symptom characteristics (including onset, duration, type, location, triggers, relieving factors, time of day) is recommended. I C

data.Table Header: Recommendation Table 1 -Recommendations for history taking, risk factor assessment, and resting electrocardiogram in individuals with suspected chronic coronary syndrome (see also Evidence Table 1)
data.Section Header: History taking and risk factor assessment
data.Recommendations: Symptoms like chest pain triggered by emotional stress; dyspnoea or dizziness on exertion; pain in the arms, jaw, neck, or upper back; or fatigue should be considered as potential angina equivalents.18,33,57,59,77 IIa B

data.Table Header: Recommendation Table 1 -Recommendations for history taking, risk factor assessment, and resting electrocardiogram in individuals with suspected chronic coronary syndrome (see also Evidence Table 1)
data.Recommendations: If clinical or ECG assessment suggests ACS rather than CCS, immediate referral to the emergency department and/or repeated measurement of blood troponin, preferably using high-sensitivity or ultrasensitive assays, to rule out acute myocardial injury, is recommended.78,79 I B

data.Table Header: Recommendation Table 1 -Recommendations for history taking, risk factor assessment, and resting electrocardiogram in individuals with suspected chronic coronary syndrome (see also Evidence Table 1)
data.Recommendations: A resting 12-lead ECG is recommended in all individuals reporting chest pain (unless an obvious non-cardiac cause is identified), particularly during, or immediately after, an episode suggestive of myocardial ischaemia. I C

data.Table Header: Recommendation Table 1 -Recommendations for history taking, risk factor assessment, and resting electrocardiogram in individuals with suspected chronic coronary syndrome (see also Evidence Table 1)
data.Recommendations: Using ST-segment deviations during supraventricular tachyarrhythmias, particularly during re-entrant atrioventricular tachycardias, per se, as reliable evidence of obstructive CAD, is not recommended.80–84 III B
